description: List fragment information. By default, lists fragment catalog information (catalog number, cycle, time, and fragment count). Use the catalog keyword to list all fragments at a specific catalog number, or the id keyword to list the complete history of a specific fragment.
notes: Default (no keywords): Lists catalog overview - all catalog numbers with cycle, time, and fragment count
catalog <i>: Lists all fragments in a specific catalog - detailed snapshot
id <i>: Lists complete history of a specific fragment - evolution tracking
Catalog number increments each time fragments are computed
Fragment ID is unique within a catalog but may change between catalogs
Volume is the total volume of all bodies in the fragment
Body count is the number of balls/clumps in the fragment
Position is the centroid of the fragment (average position of bodies)
Requires fragment persistence (persist true) for historical data
Related commands: fragment compute, fragment activate, fragment register, fragment clear
The same fragment ID in different catalogs may be different physical clusters; use fragment list id <i> to trace one fragment through time.
No direct Python SDK method for fragment list output
Must use command interface: itasca.command('fragment list')
Can query individual fragment IDs: ball.fragment(), clump.fragment()
Can build custom Python analysis iterating over bodies
fragment list provides formatted output, Python gives programmatic access

keywords.name: catalog
keywords.description: List the fragment information of all active fragments in catalog i . This includes the fragment ID, volume, body count, and position.

keywords.name: id
keywords.description: List the catalog numbers, cycles numbers, times, volumes, body counts, and positions of the fragment with ID i .

examples.description:
List all catalog entries (overview of all fragment computations). Use case: See when fragments were computed and how many existed at each time. Output example: Catalog 1: Cycle 0, Time 0.0, 10 fragments
Catalog 2: Cycle 1000, Time 0.1, 15 fragments.

List all fragments in catalog 1 (detailed snapshot at that computation). Use case: Examine specific fragment configuration at a particular moment. Output example: Fragment 1: Volume 0.05, Bodies 5, Position (1.0, 2.0, 0.0)
Fragment 2: Volume 0.08, Bodies 8, Position (5.0, 3.0, 0.0).

List complete history of fragment 1 across all catalogs. Use case: Track how a specific fragment evolved over time. Output example: Catalog 1: Cycle 0, Time 0.0, Volume 0.05, Bodies 5
Catalog 2: Cycle 1000, Time 0.1, Volume 0.06, Bodies 6.

examples.command:
fragment compute
fragment list
model cycle 1000
fragment compute
fragment list
examples.description: Compute, list, run cycles, recompute, list again to compare. Use case: Track fragment evolution between two simulation states.

examples.command:
fragment activate cycles 100
model cycle 5000
fragment list
examples.description: Auto-compute during cycling, then list all catalog entries. Use case: See complete history of fragment evolution during auto-computation.

examples.command:
fragment list
fragment list catalog 5
fragment list id 3
examples.description: Overview, then specific catalog detail, then specific fragment history. Use case: Progressive drill-down into fragment data.
